explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means 'on one's own initiative,' 'independently,' or 'by oneself.' It is equivalent to 'on one's own account' and is widely used in both professional and personal contexts. It is grammatically invariable regardless of the subject's gender or number.

examples.en_text: I decided to leave the company and now I work on my own.
examples.target_text: Decidi sair da empresa e agora trabalho por conta própria.

examples.en_text: She learned to play the piano on her own, without any teacher's help.
examples.target_text: Ela aprendeu a tocar piano por conta própria, sem ajuda de nenhum professor.

examples.en_text: You are already eighteen years old, you need to make your decisions on your own.
examples.target_text: Você já tem dezoito anos, precisa tomar suas decisões por conta própria.

examples.en_text: Instead of hiring an agency, we organized the whole trip on our own.
examples.target_text: Em vez de contratar uma agência, nós organizamos toda a viagem por conta própria.

examples.en_text: The computer was having problems, but I managed to fix it on my own.
examples.target_text: O computador estava com problemas, mas eu consegui consertá-lo por conta própria.

examples.en_text: The children are already very independent and do their homework on their own.
examples.target_text: As crianças já são bem independentes e fazem as tarefas por conta própria.

explanation_en: This transition phrase translates to 'the fact is that' or 'the truth of the matter is.' It is used to introduce a definitive statement, clarify a situation, or get straight to the point. It is highly versatile and fits well in both formal debates and casual conversations.

examples.en_text: The fact is that we need more time to finish this project.
examples.target_text: O fato é que nós precisamos de mais tempo para terminar este projeto.

examples.en_text: I like the city a lot, but the fact is that the cost of living here is very high.
examples.target_text: Eu gosto muito da cidade, mas o fato é que o custo de vida aqui é muito alto.

examples.en_text: The fact is that if you don't sleep well, you won't be able to concentrate tomorrow.
examples.target_text: O fato é que, se você não dormir bem, não vai conseguir se concentrar amanhã.

examples.en_text: He says he is going to save money, but the fact is that he keeps spending a lot of money.
examples.target_text: Ele diz que vai economizar, mas o fato é que ele continua gastando muito dinheiro.

examples.en_text: The fact is that learning a new language requires a lot of patience and daily practice.
examples.target_text: O fato é que aprender uma nova língua exige muita paciência e prática diária.

examples.en_text: We wanted to travel over the weekend, but the fact is that it is going to rain every day.
examples.target_text: Queríamos viajar no fim de semana, mas o fato é que vai chover todos os dias.

explanation_en: This phrase means 'in a good mood' or 'good-tempered.' It is typically paired with the verb 'estar' to denote a temporary state, though it can also describe a general disposition. The antonym is 'de mau humor' (in a bad mood).

examples.en_text: My father always wakes up in a good mood and singing.
examples.target_text: O meu pai acorda sempre de bom humor e a cantar.

examples.en_text: Take the opportunity to talk to the boss now, because he seems to be in a good mood.
examples.target_text: Aproveita para falar com o chefe agora, porque ele parece estar de bom humor.

examples.en_text: When it's sunny, I immediately get in a good mood.
examples.target_text: Quando está sol, eu fico logo de bom humor.

examples.en_text: Despite the horrible traffic, she arrived at the party in a good mood.
examples.target_text: Apesar do trânsito horrível, ela chegou à festa de bom humor.

examples.en_text: I don't know what happened, but today I'm not in a good mood for jokes.
examples.target_text: Não sei o que aconteceu, mas hoje não estou de bom humor para brincadeiras.

examples.en_text: Doing physical exercise helps me stay in a good mood during the day.
examples.target_text: Praticar exercício físico ajuda-me a manter-me de bom humor durante o dia.

explanation_en: This conjunction means 'so much so that' or 'to the extent that' and is used to introduce a consequence that proves or illustrates a previous statement. It is a very natural way to link ideas in Portuguese and is common in both spoken and written registers. Learners should avoid confusing it with 'tanto quanto,' which means 'as much as.'

examples.en_text: I was very tired yesterday, so much so that I fell asleep on the couch before dinner.
examples.target_text: Eu estava muito cansado ontem, tanto que dormi no sofá antes do jantar.

examples.en_text: She liked the cake, so much so that she ate three slices.
examples.target_text: Ela gostou do bolo, tanto que comeu três fatias.

examples.en_text: It rained a lot at night, so much so that some streets were flooded.
examples.target_text: Choveu muito à noite, tanto que algumas ruas ficaram inundadas.

examples.en_text: He studied hard for the exam, so much so that he got the maximum grade.
examples.target_text: Ele estudou bastante para o exame, tanto que tirou a nota máxima.

examples.en_text: We get along very well, so much so that we travel together every year.
examples.target_text: Nós nos damos muito bem, tanto que viajamos juntos todos os anos.

examples.en_text: The city has grown in recent years, so much so that it now has a new shopping mall.
examples.target_text: A cidade cresceu nos últimos anos, tanto que agora tem um novo shopping.

explanation_en: This expression means 'to suggest' or 'to give the idea' of something. It is followed by the preposition 'de' when specifying the action or concept suggested. It is a common, natural alternative to the more formal verb 'sugerir' in everyday spoken Portuguese.

examples.en_text: Who suggested having a picnic in the park?
examples.target_text: Quem é que deu a ideia de fazermos um piquenique no parque?

examples.en_text: The way she spoke gave the impression that she didn't want to go to the party.
examples.target_text: A forma como ela falou deu a ideia de que não queria ir à festa.

examples.en_text: I suggested changing the meeting date to next week.
examples.target_text: Eu dei a ideia de mudar a data da reunião para a próxima semana.

examples.en_text: Those dark colors make the room seem smaller than it actually is.
examples.target_text: Essas cores escuras dão a ideia de que o quarto é menor do que realmente é.

examples.en_text: It was my brother who suggested buying this used car.
examples.target_text: Foi o meu irmão que deu a ideia de comprarmos este carro usado.

examples.en_text: The silence in the house gave the impression that no one was there.
examples.target_text: O silêncio na casa dava a ideia de que não estava lá ninguém.

explanation_en: This construction uses the verb 'acabar' in the past participle followed by 'de' and an infinitive to express that an action has 'just' occurred. In European Portuguese, 'ter acabado de + infinitive' is the standard way to express the immediate past, whereas Brazilian Portuguese often uses 'acabar de + inflected verb' (e.g., 'ele acabou de sair'). Here, 'tinha acabado de sair' represents the pluperfect 'had just left/gotten out.'

examples.en_text: The warm bread, fresh out of the oven, smelled incredibly good.
examples.target_text: O pão quente, acabado de sair do forno, cheirava incrivelmente bem.

examples.en_text: As a young man just out of university, he had many doubts about the future.
examples.target_text: Como um jovem acabado de sair da universidade, ele tinha muitas dúvidas sobre o futuro.

examples.en_text: They were excited, having just left the cinema after watching the new movie.
examples.target_text: Eles estavam animados, acabados de sair do cinema depois de ver o novo filme.

examples.en_text: Sorry about the wet hair, I've just got out of the shower.
examples.target_text: Desculpa o cabelo molhado, estou acabado de sair do banho.

examples.en_text: We have breaking news, fresh out of the newsroom.
examples.target_text: Temos uma notícia de última hora, acabada de sair da redação.

examples.en_text: The passenger, having just got off the plane, was desperately looking for his bags.
examples.target_text: O passageiro, acabado de sair do avião, procurava desesperadamente pelas suas malas.

explanation_en: 'Baita' is a highly common colloquial adjective in Brazilian Portuguese, particularly in the South and Southeast regions, used to intensify nouns. It is equivalent to 'enorme' (huge) or 'grande' (great) and is placed before the noun it modifies. While informal, it is frequently heard in everyday conversations, media, and informal political commentary.

examples.en_text: Yesterday I got a huge surprise when I arrived home.
examples.target_text: Ontem recebi uma baita surpresa quando cheguei em casa.

examples.en_text: That doctor is a great professional, he helped my family a lot.
examples.target_text: Aquele médico é um baita profissional, ele ajudou muito a minha família.

examples.en_text: We got stuck in a huge traffic jam on the highway because of the accident.
examples.target_text: Pegamos um baita trânsito na estrada por causa do acidente.

examples.en_text: Last night there was a huge rainstorm and the power went out.
examples.target_text: Ontem à noite caiu uma baita chuva e acabou a energia.

examples.en_text: This job opening is a great opportunity for your career.
examples.target_text: Essa vaga de emprego é uma baita oportunidade para a sua carreira.

examples.en_text: What a scare! You gave me a huge fright appearing out of nowhere.
examples.target_text: Que susto! Você me deu um baita susto aparecendo do nada.

explanation_en: This compound noun literally translates to 'rain-sender' but is used colloquially to mean the 'big boss,' 'head honcho,' or 'influential leader' of a group or organization. It has a slightly informal, sometimes mildly cynical tone, suggesting someone who holds all the power and makes all the decisions. It is invariable in gender ('o manda-chuva', 'a manda-chuva') and pluralizes as 'os manda-chuvas'.

examples.en_text: If you want a raise, you need to speak directly with the big boss of the company.
examples.target_text: Se você quer um aumento, precisa falar diretamente com o manda-chuva da empresa.

examples.en_text: Who is the head honcho around here? I need authorization to park the car.
examples.target_text: Quem é o manda-chuva por aqui? Preciso de autorização para estacionar o carro.

examples.en_text: She is the new big boss of the marketing department, so all decisions go through her.
examples.target_text: Ela é a nova manda-chuva do departamento de marketing, então todas as decisões passam por ela.

examples.en_text: Even though he thinks he's in charge of everything, the real head honcho is the financial director.
examples.target_text: Apesar de ele achar que manda em tudo, o verdadeiro manda-chuva é o diretor financeiro.

examples.en_text: It's no use complaining to the employees, you have to talk to the big bosses.
examples.target_text: Não adianta reclamar com os funcionários, você tem que falar com os manda-chuvas.

examples.en_text: She started as an intern and today she is the head honcho of the whole organization.
examples.target_text: Ela começou como estagiária e hoje é a manda-chuva de toda a organização.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to lie down and roll over,' this idiomatic expression means to do exactly as one pleases, to have a field day, or to take full advantage of a situation without any opposition. It is often used when someone exploits a position of power or a weak opponent to their heart's content. It carries an informal register and is highly expressive in political and sports commentary.

examples.en_text: Since the boss is very calm, the team does whatever they want and nobody works seriously.
examples.target_text: Como o chefe é muito calmo, a equipe deita e rola e ninguém trabalha sério.

examples.en_text: The striker had a field day in yesterday's game because the opposing defense was very weak.
examples.target_text: O atacante deitou e rolou no jogo de ontem porque a defesa adversária estava muito fraca.

examples.en_text: If you leave the kids alone in the kitchen, they will have a field day with the sweets.
examples.target_text: Se você deixar as crianças sozinhas na cozinha, elas vão deitar e rolar com os doces.

examples.en_text: The competition is having a field day because our company stopped investing in advertising.
examples.target_text: A concorrência está deitando e rolando porque a nossa empresa parou de investir em propaganda.

examples.en_text: The guests had a field day at the party, since the food and drinks were free.
examples.target_text: Os convidados deitaram e rolaram na festa, já que a comida e a bebida eram de graça.

examples.en_text: You need to set boundaries, otherwise people will walk all over you.
examples.target_text: Você precisa impor limites, senão as pessoas deitam e rolam em cima de você.

explanation_en: This common phrase means to change the subject, digress, or dodge a topic during a conversation. It is composed of the verb 'desviar' (to deflect/divert) and the prepositional phrase 'do assunto' (from the subject). It is an essential conversational tool for advanced learners to describe when someone is avoiding a direct question or when a discussion is getting off track.

examples.en_text: Whenever I ask about his plans, he tries to change the subject.
examples.target_text: Sempre que pergunto sobre os planos dele, ele tenta desviar do assunto.

examples.en_text: Let's not get off track; we need to decide this today.
examples.target_text: Não vamos desviar do assunto; precisamos decidir isso hoje.

examples.en_text: She noticed that he changed the subject when she mentioned the money.
examples.target_text: Ela percebeu que ele desviou do assunto quando ela mencionou o dinheiro.

examples.en_text: Why are you changing the subject? Are you hiding something?
examples.target_text: Por que você está desviando do assunto? Está escondendo alguma coisa?

examples.en_text: The politician tried to dodge the question during the interview, but the journalist insisted.
examples.target_text: O político tentou desviar do assunto durante a entrevista, mas o jornalista insistiu.

examples.en_text: If you change the subject now, they will think you are guilty.
examples.target_text: Se você desviar do assunto agora, eles vão achar que você é culpado.

explanation_en: In political and social contexts, 'fazer um jogo' means to play a strategic game, put on an act, or behave deceptively to achieve a specific goal. It implies that the person's public stance or actions are calculated maneuvers rather than genuine beliefs. It is a versatile collocation used to analyze behavior, negotiations, and public relations.

examples.en_text: They never say what they really think; they always play a game to get what they want.
examples.target_text: Eles nunca dizem o que realmente pensam; fazem sempre um jogo para conseguir o que querem.

examples.en_text: If the weather is good on Saturday, we will play a game of football with friends.
examples.target_text: Se o tempo estiver bom no sábado, fazemos um jogo de futebol com os amigos.

examples.en_text: In that company, people play a very complicated political game to get promoted.
examples.target_text: Naquela empresa, as pessoas fazem um jogo político muito complicado para subir de cargo.

examples.en_text: I think she is not being sincere with you; she is just playing a game to see your reaction.
examples.target_text: Acho que ela não está a ser sincera contigo, ela só faz um jogo para ver a tua reação.

examples.en_text: Every Friday night, we play a card game as a family.
examples.target_text: Todas as sextas-feiras à noite, nós fazemos um jogo de cartas em família.

examples.en_text: The two directors are playing a power game to see who makes the final decision.
examples.target_text: Os dois diretores fazem um jogo de poder para ver quem toma a decisão final.

explanation_en: While 'marchar' literally means to march, 'marchar com' is used figuratively in political and social contexts to mean aligning with, supporting, or being in step with a particular group, ideology, or leader. It suggests a coordinated movement or shared path. This expression is common in journalistic and analytical registers when discussing alliances.

examples.en_text: Our team is aligning with the board's new decisions.
examples.target_text: Nossa equipe está marchando com as novas decisões da diretoria.

examples.en_text: The representative guaranteed that he is in step with the population's wishes.
examples.target_text: O deputado garantiu que está marchando com os desejos da população.

examples.en_text: I feel that I am finally aligning with my own values and not with those of others.
examples.target_text: Sinto que finalmente estou marchando com os meus próprios valores e não com os dos outros.

examples.en_text: If we don't keep in step with current technology, we are going to lose many customers.
examples.target_text: Se não marcharmos com a tecnologia atual, vamos perder muitos clientes.

examples.en_text: The teachers are supporting the school's new pedagogical project.
examples.target_text: Os professores estão marchando com o novo projeto pedagógico da escola.

examples.en_text: The whole family ended up going along with the decision to sell the old house.
examples.target_text: Toda a família acabou marchando com a decisão de vender a casa antiga.
